source.title: A Heuristic for Unsupervised Model Selection for Variational Disentangled Representation Learning
source.authors: Sunny Duan; L. Matthey; Andre Saraiva; Nicholas Watters; Christopher P. Burgess; Alexander Lerchner; I. Higgins

record.tranche_reason: Measures similarity across independently initialized models of the same VAE class using pairwise latent comparisons, rather than testing convergence with model scale or the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The study directly compares representations across seeds within model classes and describes how similarity differs between high-, medium-, and low-UDR models. Results cited from other papers about representation convergence are not counted. UDR correlations with supervised scores are included only where they compare similarity-measure variants relevant to metric dependence; general disentanglement scores and task-performance results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly a model-selection method (UDR), but UDR is itself a cross-seed similarity score for same-architecture VAEs. Appendix A.10 and A.9 check by latent traversals whether independently seeded models converge to the same axis-aligned factors. That bears on V3 with a different method from Li et al. The check is partly circular: models are grouped by UDR, which is already a cross-seed similarity score. No row measures convergence across architectures, modalities, scale, or under varied similarity measures.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly wrong emphasis. The authors mainly conclude that UDR, an unsupervised pairwise model-comparison score, matches supervised disentanglement metrics for model and hyperparameter selection across 5400 models, and predicts fairness and RL data efficiency. The idea that disentangled models are alike and entangled ones differ is their assumption, which they verify qualitatively. They caution it may not hold for other model classes.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes UDR, a pairwise latent-response similarity and ranking method for disentanglement selection; it does not reproduce the original convergence studies’ methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Similarity matrix method (Lasso versus Spearman), within-hyperparameter versus all-to-all model pairing, number of pairwise comparisons P, and dataset/model class. The reported average correlations are similar for Lasso and Spearman; pairwise-comparison count affects correlation and variance.

fits_no_version.finding: Agreement of UDR rankings with supervised disentanglement metrics: Lasso vs Spearman similarity, within-hyperparameter vs all-to-all pools, and the number of pairwise comparisons P. Correlations range 0.51–0.61.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Rankings by cross-seed latent similarity track supervised disentanglement scores, largely insensitive to the similarity estimator.

record.code_released: not stated (code said to be released as part of disentanglement_lib; no URL given)
record.problems: The cross-seed convergence evidence is primarily qualitative latent-traversal inspection, with no numeric direct similarity values for the plotted model pairs. Comparisons are largely within a model class and dataset, and high/low grouping is based on the proposed UDR score itself. The study explicitly notes UDR assumptions and limitations, including dependence on the pool of comparison models, sensitivity to latent-factor properties, and a bias toward models learning subsets of factors.
record.rows_left_out: None. The main tables comparing UDR with supervised disentanglement metrics are omitted unless they compare UDR similarity-measure variants; they assess metric-ranking agreement rather than representation convergence itself.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep and no cross-architecture, cross-objective or cross-data comparison; all models share one small conv VAE architecture.
Lasso maps between latents are used only inside the similarity score; mapping loss, stitching, relative representations and unpaired mapping are not evaluated.
No formal comparison of features across model classes. Fig. 15 colour-codes similar factors in three classes but makes no cross-class claim. No neurons, SAE features or circuits.
Convergence magnitude is not compared across similarity measures or input distributions. Lasso and Spearman variants are compared only by their agreement with supervised metrics.
Neither a plateau nor the causes of convergence are tested.

missing.what: UDR score distributions over 50 seeds per hyperparameter setting. This is a direct quantitative cross-seed similarity measure: β=1 vanilla VAEs score low, and no DIP-VAE-I, DIP-VAE-II or FactorVAE model on dSprites scores highly.
Low-UDR (<0.3) β-VAE groups on CelebA and ImageNet, described as less interpretable and not similar across models.

record.verdict_notes: The cross-seed similarity evidence is qualitative and partly circular, because models are binned by the cross-seed similarity score itself. Rows r13–r25 are method-validation numbers and should be unlinked from V6.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep, nor comparisons across different architectures, objectives, data, or modalities to test convergence with scale.
No paired image-caption vision/language representation comparison.
Tests different seeds within the same model class, principally through qualitative latent traversals and UDR comparisons. Does not test whether particular individual units or bases match.

Uses Lasso-based similarity as one component of UDR, but does not test whether one model’s representations can be mapped to another’s with little loss or evaluate stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
Qualitatively compares interpretable latent factors across models. Does not test recurrence of individual neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
Varies similarity measure, comparison pool, and number of pairwise comparisons; does not systematically vary input distributions or test out-of-distribution convergence.
Does not test whether convergence plateaus or whether shared training data/objectives cause alignment rather than a common model of reality.

rows.operation_detail: Compared latent traversals across independently seeded models with high UDR scores.
rows.measure: Qualitative similarity and interpretability of latent representations across models
rows.value: The representations appear interpretable and similar up to permutation, sign inversion, and subsetting.
rows.note: The accompanying text explicitly describes the plotted representations as similar; no numeric pairwise similarity is reported.
rows.check: Seeds share architecture and class, so this is V3, not V5. The band is chosen by UDR (cross-seed similarity), so the similarity is partly a selection effect.

relationships.condition: High-UDR seeds of β-VAE, TC-VAE and CCI-VAE on dSprites (UDR>0.4), and β-VAE on CelebA (UDR>0.6)
relationships.reason: Traversals show the same interpretable factors across seeds, up to permutation, sign and subsetting (r1–r3, r11). The grouping is by UDR itself, so this is partly a selection effect.
relationships.display_finding: Selected seeds recovered the same interpretable factors up to permutation, sign and subsetting, although selection by UDR partly accounts for this agreement.

relationships.condition: Medium/low-UDR models (FactorVAE, DIP-VAE-I/II, low-β settings) and β-VAE on ImageNet
relationships.reason: Seeds with the same architecture learn less similar or clearly different representations in these groups (r4–r10), and only coarse shared structure on ImageNet (r12). Cross-seed convergence therefore depends on model class and hyperparameter regime.
relationships.display_finding: Several model groups showed weaker coordinate alignment across seeds, while ImageNet β-VAE models shared coarse structure.

relation.reason: A.10 explicitly evaluates the similarity assumption with model traversals; the study does more than use convergence for model selection.

tranche.reason: The study qualitatively checks cross-seed representation similarity using latent traversals alongside its pairwise UDR method.

source_check.notes: A.2 explicitly distinguishes UDR's axis alignment from affine-invariant representation comparisons. High-UDR similarity is selected by the score itself, and subsetting permits models representing few factors to score highly.

statements.correction: Medium/low-UDR groups have less similar or different coordinate traversals. Shared-subspace convergence under different bases is untested. High-UDR ImageNet models have more similar representations despite coarse information and poor reconstruction.
statements.problem: The traversal descriptions are accurate, but dependence of broad V3 convergence is not established: UDR tests axis alignment, and ImageNet coarseness concerns represented information rather than cross-seed similarity.
